chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated from 'Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Takbir, and he said: 'It is obligatory after every obligatory or voluntary prayer during the days of Tashriq.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning is that it is strongly recommended (mustahabb), not that it is a mandatory duty (fard) for which the one who leaves it deserves punishment. This is indicated by the narrations we have previously mentioned, and what clarifies it further is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيق: Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Takbir after prayers during the days of Tashriq in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam designates the Takbir after prayers during the Days of Tashriq as 'obligatory' (wajib), a ruling clarified by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan as denoting strong recommendation (shadid al-istihbab) rather than a penal mandatory duty (fard). This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance where high spiritual merit is accorded to this specific dhikr without imposing the strict liability of omission found in core pillars of prayer. The practice serves as a public proclamation of Allah's greatness, reinforcing the festive spirit of Eid al-Adha within the ritual framework.
